Hero V4 — two clocks

The process line is gone from the background — it and its tributaries were the clutter. The city stays, under two scrims, rebuilt in two depth layers. The journey moves into the panel, where it is information rather than decoration. And the panel now shows what a prospect actually wants: two clocks — yours and the NYPD’s — because the NYPD’s ~6 months is identical on every track and your half is the part that differs. What changed, and why

The clutter was the process lineThe route and its tributaries crossing the buildings were doing the damage — two competing line systems in the same space. Deleting it fixed more than tuning it would have. The city alone is calm, and unmistakably New York.
Two scrims, not oneA global veil so nothing competes with the type, plus a left-weighted one under the copy column. Lifted again over the lower band so the skyline still reads — the first pass buried it entirely.
Your repo already answered the timeline questioncontent/facts.ts and /timeline carry attorney-approved, sourced copy: “Two clocks run here, not one.” The NYPD’s is roughly six months from a complete submission. That framing is better than a single invented number, and it is already signed off.
Why the reference count is the real per-track numberThe NYPD’s six months is identical on all three tracks. What changes is your half — and what drives your half is how many people you have to chase: four notarized references, two, or none. That turns 4 / 2 / 0 from trivia into the thing that actually moves your date.
The dead row is gone“13 stages” was identical on every track, which made it noise in a panel whose whole job is to differentiate. Replaced by the clock split, the chase count, and what proves your standing — three rows, all meaningful.
⚠ The prep ranges need sign-offThe ~6 months is sourced and attorney-approved. 8–12 / 6–9 / 4–6 weeks are placeholders. They must be approved or dropped to qualitative language before this ships — the build prompt makes that blocking, and the panel already carries a footnote saying the prep range is an estimate, not a promise.
